A 84-year-old male presents with an 8-month history of fatigue. He reports that he previously walked 2
miles daily but now becomes fatigued after less than half a mile and experiences shortness of breath
when climbing one flight of stairs. His medical history includes hypertension and osteoarthritis, and his
medications are lisinopril, aspirin, and occasional tylenol for pain. He denies weight loss, visible blood
in his stool or urine, and dark stools. His last colonoscopy, performed 8 years ago, revealed benign
polyps that were removed. Vital signs show a temperature of 37.2°C (98.9°F), pulse of 115/min,
respiratory rate of 18/min, and blood pressure of 153/91 mmHg. On physical examination, conjunctival
pallor, pale nail beds, dry skin, and tachycardia with a regular rhythm are noted. Lungs are clear to
auscultation, and the abdominal exam is normal. Laboratory results are as follows: | **Laboratory
value** | **Result** | | --- | --- | | Hemoglobin | 8.5 g/dL | | Hematocrit | 32% | | MCV | 72 fL | | Fecal
occult blood test | Negative | | Iron | 38 μg/dL | | Ferritin | 12 ng/mL | What is the most appropriate next
step in management? Answer Choices: (A) CT scan abdomen (B) Capsule endoscopy (C)
Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) (D) Reticulocyte count analysis (E) Packed red blood cell
transfusion (F) Colonoscopy (G) Bone marrow biopsy (H) Oral iron supplementation (I) Peripheral
blood smear (J) IV iron supplementation
 A. Oral iron supplementation
B. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD)
C. Peripheral blood smear

D. IV iron supplementation
E. Bone marrow biopsy
F. CT scan abdomen
G. Reticulocyte count analysis
H. Packed red blood cell transfusion
I. Colonoscopy
J. Capsule endoscopy
